name: Wine Brown
lede: Wine Brown is a dark, reddish brown whose own naming origin is undocumented in our sources, and whose nearest match in our data, [[wine-brown|Dusty Wine]], measures as essentially the same color.

sections.title: Origin undocumented
sections.body:
Our sources flag Wine Brown as coming through a Japanese color list, though the name itself reads as a plain English compound of "wine" and "brown"; who coined it and when is not documented here [1]. [[wine-brown|Dusty Wine]] sits at a measured distance of 0.0 units, meaning the two names point at effectively the same swatch in our data [1]. Beyond that near-duplicate, its closest distinct look-alikes are Rubient, read as more vivid, and Black-Red, read as darker [1].

A separate, unrelated Japanese traditional color, Murasakitobi (紫鳶, literally "purple kite"), sits in a similarly dark reddish-purple-brown range; our data does not claim any link between that name and Wine Brown's own origin, but the two make a useful comparison across naming traditions [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds this color in 232 of them, 0.98 percent, as photographed, more common than 64 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 1.4 percent of that century's works, 1.8 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in 57 percent of its appearances, found by close reading rather than at a glance [2].

The earliest match is a 1405 panel by Starnina (Gherardo di Jacopo); our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from Germany, 2.4 times the expected rate, and in printed English the word rose fastest in the 1860s, across all its senses [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented (a plain English compound: wine + brown)
